headline: Valon, a start-up whose AI software runs mortgage servicing, has raised $150 million at a value of $2.3 billion, double its previous value.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score of 5: a sizeable AI-software round in mortgage servicing, but the figures are the company's own.
importance_line: What changed is that a start-up selling AI agents to mortgage servicers has doubled its valuation and added a major new investor, which matters to homeowners whose loans may run on its system, then to lenders and servicers weighing a move to new software, then to rival software vendors, and the doubt is that the revenue and coverage figures are the company's own and the report does not say how much of the work the AI agents actually do.
summary: HousingWire reports that Valon Technologies, whose AI-based software runs mortgage servicing (collecting payments and managing accounts on home loans), raised $150 million in a Series D round (a later-stage funding round) at a $2.3 billion valuation, double its previous one, with new investor Ribbit Capital joining existing backer Andreessen Horowitz, the company said on Monday 5 Oct 2026. Valon says it has more than $200 million in contracted annual recurring revenue (yearly subscription income) and is under contract to power servicing for roughly one in six outstanding US mortgages, and it plans to spend the money on product development and hiring.
notes: Full HousingWire article read; revenue and coverage figures are the company's own. 'Monday' is 5 Oct 2026.
